thread:
cs-anna: FYI high-sev from customer Savvie — they started seeing 502/504s from our hosted endpoint around 09:02 UTC, intermittent but now persistent. Customer reports many timeouts and degraded p95, sending examples. escalation ticket #E-4982.
cs-anna: sample request ids: req=rs-H5k2, rs-H5k3, rs-H5k6. They say failures started right after a spike in long-context summarization jobs.
cs-ops: attaching snippet from their support dump: 
```
502 GatewayTimeout: upstream request timed out
route=/v1/generate model=redwood-large context_len=12000 tokens_out=2048
proxy_queue_depth=4989 batcher_backlog=137
```
cs-anna: they also reported a billed spike; not sure if related but they escalated billing because of retries.
sam (oncall): jumping in — hitting 5xx/gateway from hosted inference, sounds like queue saturation / tail latency. Are there platform alerts?
sre-bot: alert: request-queue-depth > 4500 on hosted-us-east-1 (last 5m). p95 latency > 2.1s, 504 count increased by 420% in 10m.
alex: looking at metrics now — we see a sustained increase in queue depth across multiple gateway nodes for tenant Savvie, but oddly requests appear to hop between nodes (routing logs show request forwarded to another gateway with same request-id). Could be double-enqueue or requeue loop.
maya (eng-runtime): I saw a canary rollout last night to change continuous-batching config (commit b7f3d2) that increased max_batch_delay from 20ms -> 60ms to improve throughput on steady small requests. That could increase worst-case tail latency when combined with many long-running calls.
alex: checking batcher logs for host pool: 
```
[2026-03-15T08:59:12Z] batcher: enqueue req=rs-H5k2, tenant=savvie, seq=1 len=12000
[2026-03-15T08:59:12Z] batcher: batch_size=1 delay=60ms waiting to aggregate
[2026-03-15T09:00:05Z] worker: long-prediction started req=rs-H5k2 tokens_out=2048 duration_est=18s
[2026-03-15T09:00:05Z] batcher: backlog=129, queue_depth=4621
```
alex: the problem seems compounded: long-context requests are monopolizing workers, and because we wait up to 60ms to batch, the batching window groups few long requests and increases end-to-end. We're also seeing gateway routing retries that re-enqueue the same request instead of failing fast.
cs-ops: customer is getting charged for the retries; they filed billing dispute. We should give them mitigation asap.
sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) tenant-level ingress throttle (reduce concurrency), 2) lower max_batch_delay back to 20ms, 3) redirect tenant to a dedicated pool if available, 4) temporary per-tenant token cap. Which can we do now?
maya: I can roll back the max_batch_delay change in canary to stop increasing tail latency. Rolling back will be quick (config flip) — doing a canary rollout now and will observe.
deploy-bot: deploy initiated: config-revert max_batch_delay->20ms by maya at 09:05 UTC (deploy id d-8923).
sam: while that's rolling, I'm applying a tenant ingress rule to clamp Savvie concurrency to 20 active requests to stop queue growth. Applying now.
sre-bot: action: tenant-rate-limit applied for tenant=savvie concurrency=20 TTL=30m.
alex: after rate-limit and rollback, queue depth dropped from 4700 -> 800 in ~90s and 504s reduced by ~78% in 4m. Good short-term result.
cs-anna: communicated mitigation to Savvie support and offered to reverse invoice for retry traffic while we investigate root cause. They want a postmortem.
maya: next steps for root cause: 1) reproduce a mixed workload of long-context heavy requests + bursts of small requests in staging with max_batch_delay=60ms, 2) validate gateway re-enqueue logic for transient failures (I suspect a bug where 502 triggers a requeue loop if proxy timeout occurs), 3) add per-tenant backpressure (token-based) as permanent control.
alex: reproducible repro steps I used locally: 
```
1) spawn 120 concurrent clients for tenant 'savvie' sending summarize jobs with context_len ~12k tokens, token_out=2k
2) send an intermittent small-chat ping every 100ms from other tenants to exercise routing
3) observe batcher backlog, worker occupancy and gateway re-queues via /debug/metrics endpoint
```
maya: found a gateway edge-case: when worker responds with early EOF (long-run preemption), gateway returned 502 and immediately retried to another gateway node because of sticky-session misflag. That creates visual "hopping" and duplicates inflight work which amplifies saturation. I'll open PR to change retry behavior to fail-fast for 5xx from worker when tenant concurrency > threshold.
ingrid (product): need to communicate SLA impact to customers and track billing remediation. cs-anna pls confirm timeline for Savvie refund.
cs-anna: told them we'll credit retry charges and provide a 72h incident update. They're OK with that for now.
alex: action items assigned: maya -> PR to hard-fail worker-502 retry; alex -> add more granular queue depth alerting per-tenant and automated throttle; sam -> run capacity scale test and evaluate dedicating a pool for Savvie; cs-ops -> finalize refund and customer comms.
cs-ops: will draft refund note and escalate to finance.
sre-bot: follow-up alert scheduled: check queue_depth reduction and 5xx rates every 5m for 1h.
cs-anna: filing postmortem ticket PM-1127 and linking logs + repro steps. We'll include timeline, impact, and billing remediation.
cs-anna: thanks everyone — will post updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
